description: A version is proposed only once it has been public for two days, so that a release pulled or fixed in its first days never reaches a branch. internalChecksFilter is already strict by default; it is stated so that the wait is read here as holding back the branch and the pull request themselves, not only a status check on them

packageRules.description: The base image is pulled by a tag that is pushed again whenever Ubuntu rebuilds it, so a checkout does not say which image a release was built from. Pinning the digest states it in the Dockerfile, and a rebuild upstream arrives as a digest update that changes the Dockerfile and so leads to the next weekly release

The official ubuntu image, which the Dockerfile is built from, is proposed without the two-day wait. Docker Hub gives a tag's last push as its release time, and the official ubuntu tags are pushed again every day or two, so a tag seldom looks two days old and an update would hardly ever be proposed. The name is matched as it is written, not as Docker Hub resolves it, so each way of writing the image is listed. The pull request's checks still have to pass

Patch, digest and pinning updates are merged by Renovate itself once the pull request's checks pass, which build the image and run test/run.sh against it. platformAutomerge is off so that the merge waits for those checks without relying on the repository's auto-merge setting or branch protection. Minor and major updates only open a pull request

Workflows are already read by the github-actions manager. Grouping them keeps a handful of actions from arriving as a handful of pull requests, since they are updated together and reviewed the same way
